title: Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the order write
rule: DB-2 (>1 write = one transaction()) + Nygard partial-failure lens
why: _stampReorderAt does its own read+write OUTSIDE the transaction that persists the order change, in both saveOrder and resetToDefault. A process death or DB error between the two calls leaves the new order committed but the overdue-amnesty stamp missing (or the delete committed but the stamp missing on resetToDefault) — the code's own comment about wrapping upserts 'so a mid-loop crash cannot leave a half-shuffled state' shows the author cared about exactly this class of bug but didn't extend it to the second write.
recommendation: Move the _stampReorderAt call inside the same _database.transaction(...) block in both saveOrder and resetToDefault.
acceptance_criteria: Test: throw inside a fake trackDao.stampReorderAt call and assert the learning_order upsert rows are also rolled back as one atomic unit
